FAQ

Questions and answers

Short answers about Apps for Nextcloud. For step-by-step fixes, see the help page.

Is this an official Nextcloud app?

No. Apps for Nextcloud is an independent app made by a single developer. It isn't affiliated with Nextcloud GmbH.

Does it work offline?

Yes. You can create and edit cards, notes and bookmarks without a connection. Your changes upload when the network comes back.

What does it do with my data?

Your data goes only to the Nextcloud server you sign in to. There are no ads, no tracking and no analytics, and you don't need an account with the developer, who receives none of your data.

The one exception to "only your server": in News, article images and feed icons load straight from the sites that publish them, as in a browser. The details are in the privacy policy.

What do I need?

A phone or tablet with Android 12 or later, and your own Nextcloud server with the apps you want to use: Deck, Notes, News or Bookmarks. Each module works on its own, so you only need the server apps you use.

There's nothing to install on the server besides those apps.

My server uses a self-signed certificate. Will it work?

Yes. Install your CA certificate on the phone, then sign in. The help page has the steps. Plain http:// also works on your local network.

Is it free?

Yes. It's free, with no ads.

Does it work with ownCloud?

No. It uses the Nextcloud apps' own APIs.

Is there an iPhone or iPad version?

Not yet. The app is on Android only for now; iOS will come later.

Why isn't it open source?

Apps for Nextcloud is a one-person side project, and the hope is that one day it pays for its own costs, perhaps through a subscription. That's why the code stays closed.

Closed code doesn't change what happens to your data: there are no ads, no tracking and no analytics, and your data goes only to the server you sign in to.

Is it on F-Droid?

No. F-Droid only takes open-source apps, and this one isn't. It's on Google Play only for now.

Was AI used to build it?

Yes. AI tools helped write the code, as they do in many apps today. Every release is tested on real devices against a real Nextcloud server.

I found a bug. Where do I report it?

Write to nextcloudapps@desarrollodroide.es with your Android version, your Nextcloud version and the steps that lead to the problem.
